content: Take this medication by mouth with food as directed by your doctor. Typically, it is taken once daily for the first two weeks, followed by three times a week for the next 22 weeks. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, age, and response to treatment. Swallow the 100-milligram tablets whole. If you are using the 20-milligram tablets and have difficulty swallowing, you may mix the dose with water or soft food as instructed. Examples of soft foods include yogurt, applesauce, mashed banana, or porridge. Ensure you consume the entire dose by rinsing the container with additional food or liquid and swallowing immediately. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are on a daily schedule, take it at the same time each day. If you are on a three-times-a-week schedule, ensure at least 48 hours between doses and take it on the same days each week (e.g., Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays) at the same time of day. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, joint pain, and headache. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Bedaquiline may cause a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it can be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that may indicate a severe allergic reaction. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before starting bedaquiline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Bedaquiline may affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation), and the risk may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also increase this risk. Conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting, or the use of certain drugs like diuretics (water pills), may further elevate this risk. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication, as it may increase the risk of liver disease. Bedaquiline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of bedaquiline from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., liver function, EKG, potassium/calcium/magnesium levels) should be performed before starting this medication and periodically during treatment. Attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a daily dose during the first two weeks of treatment, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. If you miss a dose from week three onward, take it as soon as you remember, then return to your usual three-times-a-week dosing schedule. Ensure at least 24 hours between doses and do not exceed the weekly dose within a seven-day period. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the drying agent (desiccant) in the bottle if using the 20-milligram tablets. If necessary, the 100-milligram tablets may be stored in another container for up to three months. Close the bottle tightly when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
